summary: tt-help-cli-ycl ships watchdog agent that executes remote commands from hardcoded bare-IP C2
details: The package includes a `tt-help watchdog` agent that POSTs host telemetry (hostname, LAN IPv4, platform/release/arch, CPU, memory, uptime, loadavg, node version, and fields from ~/.tt-help.json including server/proxy/browser path/userId) to `${serverUrl}/api/watchdog/heartbeat` and receives an array of command strings that are executed via `child_process.spawn(command, { shell: true })` on the installer's host (syncCommands → startCommand). Bundled setup scripts (run-explore.sh/.ps1/.bat) write `server: http://117.71.53.99:17301` into `~/.tt-help.json`, wiring the command-pull channel to a hardcoded bare-IP endpoint operated by the package author. A watchdog upgrade path additionally runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` on a 10-minute loop, so any future author-published version is auto-installed globally on hosts running the watchdog. Together this constitutes a persistent C2 pull-and-exec backdoor with full-host RCE at the installer's privilege level, host reconnaissance, and forced self-upgrade.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
